bib.title: Rephrase and Respond: Let Large Language Models Ask Better Questions for Themselves

read.skipped: References skimmed only; Fig 4/5/7 bar values are unlabeled number clouds in the text layer.

question: Can an LLM be made to answer better by first rephrasing and expanding the human's question itself, removing ambiguity between human and LLM framing?
hypothesis: LLMs have their own frames of thought that differ from humans', so questions that look clear to humans are misread; letting the LLM rephrase before answering aligns the frames and improves accuracy.
contributions: RaR: rephrase and respond in a single prompt
Two-step RaR: a rephrasing LLM passes original and rephrased question to a (possibly different) responding LLM
Comparison with zero-shot and few-shot CoT, showing RaR is complementary

method.summary: Zero-shot prompting study. One-step RaR appends 'Rephrase and expand the question, and respond.' to the question; Two-step RaR first generates a rephrasing and then answers using original plus rephrased question. Evaluated on 10 tasks with GPT-4, then GPT-4-0613, GPT-3.5-turbo-0613 and Vicuna-13b-v1.5, plus CoT comparisons.

inference.prompting: Zero-shot; one-step RaR prompt (3.1); Two-step RaR uses a rephrase prompt then a respond prompt; format prompts of Table 6 appended to both original and RaR questions. Few-shot CoT only in Sec 6.2.

parameters.gpt35_postprocessing: all sentences containing 'rephrase' removed for GPT-3.5 on Sports and Dates

other.note: Number of runs, seeds, temperature not stated.

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: Exact-match: answer correct if it contains the exact correct word and no incorrect responses; then verified and corrected by manual inspection

metrics.name: StereoSet Language Modeling Score
metrics.definition: whether the LLM selects related options over unrelated ones

metrics.name: StereoSet Fair Score
metrics.definition: proportion of responses choosing neither related option (judged that nothing can be concluded)

baselines: zero-shot CoT ('Let's think step by step.')
one-shot and four-shot CoT (Wei et al. 2022), also with flawed examples
eval.protocol: Single reported accuracy per cell; no seeds, runs or confidence intervals stated. Subsets of 220 drawn at random for tasks other than Dates (entire dataset).

availability.data: inferred: tasks are public except the Allen-Zhu & Li-style sets, which the authors regenerated with GPT-4 (footnote 1); no release stated

prompts.text: "{question}"\nRephrase and expand the question, and respond.
Reword and elaborate on the inquiry, then provide an answer.
Reframe the question with additional context and detail, then provide an answer.
Modify the original question for clarity and detail, then offer an answer.
Restate and elaborate on the inquiry before proceeding with a response.

"{question}"
Given the above question, rephrase and expand it to help you do better answering.
Maintain all information in the original question.

limits: Most tasks have only 104-369 questions; no seeds, repeated runs or confidence intervals reported.
Decoding settings (temperature, max tokens) not stated; GPT-4 API versions are dated (accessed Oct 2023).
Several datasets were generated by GPT-4 itself and not released; rephrasing is judged by accuracy only, correctness of rephrasings not measured systematically.
Per-model, per-task results for GPT-3.5 and Vicuna are only given in figures (Fig 5, 7).
Authors concede Vicuna's self-rephrased questions are low quality and more exploration is needed; GPT-3.5 and Vicuna sometimes get worse.
Conclusion mentions comparison with CoT 'through mathematical formulation', which does not appear in the text read.
RaR doubles or lengthens output tokens; cost not discussed.
